name: Marches Hub
idea: A West Marches / open-table sandbox campaign site where players post session logs and drop pins on a shared map, with each player only seeing what their characters have discovered.
description: A GM running a sandbox campaign wants players to add their own logs, wiki edits and drawings, plus a map with information pins, without wrestling a self-hosted wiki or forcing everyone onto Google/Discord accounts. Marches Hub gives each campaign a magic-link player roster, discovery-gated map pins (a pin is only visible once a character has been there), an expedition board where any player can call a session, and a rotating-roster rule set typical of West Marches play. The moat is the per-player knowledge-state permission model plus open-table scheduling rules that general wiki tools do not model.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel hobby; Supabase Postgres with row-level security for per-player visibility; Leaflet image-map for hand-drawn maps; magic-link login so players need no Google/Discord account.
why_hard_to_copy: Per-player discovery-gated visibility (row-level security over pins, logs and map layers) and open-table scheduling logic are fiddly to get right; a generic notes or wiki clone does not cover them. Small-niche community word of mouth also matters.

signals.summary: The original poster wants a campaign tool where players can add personal logs, wiki edits and uploaded drawings, plus a map with information pins for a West Marches-style sandbox. Replies complain that MediaWiki is tedious to host and update, wiki syntax slows content creation, and some players refuse to create Google/Discord/Microsoft accounts just to join.
signals.engagement: 9 replies on page 1 (all 2026-05-26), thread runs 5 pages

name: RPG Shelf
idea: A catalog for tabletop RPG collectors that tracks print books, PDFs and backer rewards together, tagged by game system, edition and line.
description: TTRPG fans keep 1,000+ books across print shelves, DriveThruRPG, itch.io and crowdfunding, and today they juggle Google Sheets, PDF folders and BoardGameGeek's RPGGeek. RPG Shelf lets you add a book by cover, ISBN or product title, matches it to a canonical product (system, edition, line, format), and answers 'do I already own this?' from your phone at the game store. The moat is a curated TTRPG product taxonomy (system, edition, line, reprints, bundles) and a fix-it flow for items missing from public databases, which generic book trackers lack.
web_delivery: Next.js PWA on Vercel hobby with Supabase Auth and Postgres; barcode lookup via the browser BarcodeDetector API with manual fallback; Open Library for ISBN metadata; offline cache so it works inside a game store.
why_hard_to_copy: The value is a hand-curated RPG product database (system and edition mapping, reprints, bundle contents) plus user-contributed corrections; a generic book scanner clone does not know that a 5e core rulebook and its revised printing are one line.

signals.summary: A poster asked how people catalog their print TTRPG books and supplements; the first replies were a Google Sheet with a tab per system, BookWyrm, PDF folders sorted by system, and a 1,600-item spreadsheet. One user said RPGGeek is okay but weak at sorting (no easy way to list only D&D) and hard to extend with missing items. Another user built a private shelf-photo scanner but will not share it because hosting, accounts and costs are a burden.
signals.engagement: 48+ posts on page 1 within five days (2026-10-02 to 2026-10-07)

satellite.name: Sheet Cleaner
satellite.what: Free page where you paste or upload your RPG Google Sheet or CSV and it matches titles to canonical products, flags duplicates and shows missing ISBNs.
satellite.why_shared: Collectors with a messy spreadsheet share before-and-after cleanups and ask for the tool in threads like the RPG.net cataloging one.
satellite.handoff: After cleanup, one click imports the matched list into an RPG Shelf account.

marketing.cold_outreach: Reply to cataloging threads with a free shelf import for the thread's spreadsheet users.

notes: Single high-engagement thread, no older corroboration checked. BoardGameGeek XML API terms restrict commercial use and now need a token, so seed the product data from Open Library plus your own curation. Crowded adjacent space (book trackers), so the RPG-specific taxonomy must be the real differentiator.
